nodes.label: End user
nodes.summary: A browser or app requesting pages, images, video segments or API calls through a CDN hostname.

nodes.label: Resolving name server
nodes.summary: The user's DNS resolver; the CDN sees its address (or the EDNS client subnet it forwards), not the user's.

nodes.label: CDN authoritative DNS
nodes.summary: Picks a cluster by global load balancing (a stable-allocation algorithm over map units and cluster capacities), then servers in it by consistent hashing; returns the first k live servers, k by popularity.

nodes.label: Load balancers (replicated)
nodes.summary: Global and local load balancing computed from real-time data on many servers in several data centers; a leader election picks whose output is used.

nodes.label: Edge cluster (PoP)
nodes.summary: A cluster of edge servers near users. Our wrapper for the components below.

nodes.label: Edge server
nodes.summary: Terminates the connection, checks its cache, and on a miss asks peers in the cluster, then a parent tier, then the origin.

nodes.label: Cache admission filter
nodes.summary: Cache-on-second-hit: two rotating Bloom filters remember recent requests, so one-hit wonders are served but not stored.

nodes.label: Edge cache store
nodes.summary: Memory and disk cache keyed by method and URI plus Vary headers (RFC 9111); evicts with a replacement policy such as LRU.

nodes.label: Cluster peers
nodes.summary: Other servers in the same cluster, asked first on a miss; Bloom-filter cache summaries can say who holds what.

nodes.label: Upper tier (parent)
nodes.summary: A parent cluster or upper-tier data center; only it contacts the origin, which raises hit ratios and concentrates origin connections.

nodes.label: Overlay routing
nodes.summary: Relays uncacheable traffic between edge and origin over chosen paths through CDN servers, for lower latency and redundancy when a path fails.

nodes.label: Purge API
nodes.summary: Purge or invalidate by URL, tag, prefix, hostname or everything; rate-limited with a token bucket. A 200 means received, not evicted.

nodes.label: Customer origin
nodes.summary: The content provider's servers; they set Cache-Control (max-age, s-maxage, stale-while-revalidate, private) and answer conditional requests.

steps.caption: The browser resolves the site's hostname, which is a CNAME to the CDN.
The CDN's DNS picks a nearby cluster from the resolver's address and returns k servers for this content.
The browser connects to one of them and sends the request.
The object is in cache and fresh; it is returned without contacting anyone else.

flows.name: A miss is filled through the tiers

steps.caption: The object is not in this server's cache.
Other servers in the cluster are asked first.
Then the parent or upper tier.
Only the upper tier fetches from the origin.
The edge stores the object only if it has been requested before (cache on second hit).
A request for a personalised page or API reaches the edge.
The edge forwards it over the overlay network.
The overlay uses the best of several paths to the origin, with spares if one fails.

flows.name: The origin is slow when content expires (failure)

steps.caption: The cached copy has expired and the origin allowed stale-while-revalidate.
One background revalidation goes to the origin with If-Modified-Since or an ETag.
Meanwhile users keep getting the stale copy instead of waiting; without the directive they would wait.
The customer purges by tag after a bad publish; the API accepts within its rate limit.
Every edge evicts or marks the objects stale; the next requests refill from the origin through the upper tier.
